fallback_agent.description: Agent to re-run this stage with once retry_limit is spent on the primary `agent` — the answer to 'the stage keeps failing, then what'. Must name an agent declared in contracts/agent.yaml; this schema cannot check that (different file), so a typo here fails at run time, not at validation. DECLARATIVE: whoever drives the DAG performs the switch, nothing in this bundle does.

fallback_model.description: Model to fall back to for this stage when the primary is unavailable. A model ID, not a profile: `model_profile` above says which ladder, this says which rung. Deliberately not enumerated — the licensed ladder is pinned in .harness/control/power-policy.json (fallback_chain) and casan-policies orchestration.model_fallback, and a second copy of the list here would drift from those without anything noticing. Note H7-5's scorer reads those two files, not this field.

compensate.description: Id of the stage that undoes this one when the pipeline rolls back — the transaction boundary H7-6 asks for, expressed per stage instead of only as a global flag. DECLARATIVE: nothing here executes it. A stage whose effects cannot actually be reversed should leave this unset rather than name a compensator that only looks like a rollback.

type.description: Edge semantics. Recognized vocabulary: 'data_flow' — sequential hand-off, the default; 'parallel' — fan-out, several parallel edges leaving one stage have no ordering between their targets; 'join' — fan-in, the target waits for every incoming join edge before it starts. Left as a free string rather than an enum ON PURPOSE: projects already running this bundle carry their own edge labels, and closing the set here would fail their existing workflow.yaml at the next reinstall — the same 'bundle owns the schema, project cannot fix it' trap this vocabulary was added to solve. Nothing in this bundle schedules the fan-out; these labels describe the DAG for whoever executes it.

gate_rules.description: What each gate outcome does to the pipeline. Declared here so the routing is inspectable config (C2) rather than control flow buried in a hook. Keys are outcome names, values are the action taken.

max_attempts.description: Attempts allowed for a SINGLE stage before the pipeline gives up on it — a different bound from max_cycles, which caps whole-pipeline loops (a run can stay inside max_cycles while one stage retries forever). Note H7-4's scorer reads orchestration.retry.max_attempts out of .harness/control/casan-policies.yaml, not this file: declaring it here bounds the DAG, it does not by itself move that score.
